destination.title: EFT control and quantum-gravity exclusion tests
destination.question: Which operational conditions or conjectural quantum-gravity criteria constrain cosmological histories, and when could they exclude an effective theory?
destination.summary: Distinguish history restrictions, theory-wide quantifiers, conditional derivations and phenomenological applications.

assumptions: TCC variants, distance/species inputs, GMC and de Sitter criteria retain their conjectural status.
Stochastic dynamics and operational control conditions require independent justification.
conventions: Universal, restricted, existential and probability-tolerance tests have different meanings.
excludes: Criterion satisfaction as sufficient UV consistency
Generalizing a large-excursion derivation to small excursions without an additional conjecture

sources.title: Quantum Breaking Bound on de Sitter and Swampland

evidence.text: Must a consistent cosmological history avoid the loss of its semiclassical de Sitter description? The paper assumes that it must, while acknowledging that a future-eternal quantum state beyond the break-time has not been excluded from first principles.

sources.title: Is the trans-Planckian censorship a swampland conjecture?

evidence.text: Does prohibiting trans-Planckian fluctuations from becoming classical constrain complete effective theories, or selected cosmological histories? An unobserved allowed history could exclude a theory and thereby restrict its observable predictions.

sources.title: Catastrophic production of slow gravitinos

evidence.text: Could quantum-gravity consistency exclude cosmological effective theories whose gravitino develops a catastrophic production episode?

sources.title: The gravitino and the swampland

evidence.text: Can the cosmological expansion be described below the quantum-gravity cutoff predicted by GMC? The paper imposes H<Λ_QG before deriving positive-energy mass bounds.

sources.title: Localized gravity, de Sitter, and the Horizon Criterion

evidence.text: Can cosmological horizons consistently define a quantum-gravity exclusion criterion when spacetime has dynamical boundaries, and what asymptotic scalar potentials would the resulting criterion constrain?

sources.title: Quantum Breaking Bound on de Sitter and Swampland

evidence.text: Compare local tachyonic growth with Hubble-scale diffusion, then test whether any resulting patch can outlive the quantum deadline. The paper uses this asymptotic comparison rather than solving a stochastic first-passage problem.

sources.title: Is the trans-Planckian censorship a swampland conjecture?

evidence.text: Start from a history-level condition, specify the realization domain, and choose the quantifier used to reject theories. Probabilistic rejection additionally requires a normalized measure and a maximum tolerated violation probability.

sources.title: Catastrophic production of slow gravitinos

evidence.text: Differentiate a scalar-dependent mass along a cosmological trajectory, combine its Kähler and superpotential derivatives, and rewrite the result using field-space contractions. Preserve trajectory and phase assumptions when forming the simplified output.

sources.title: The gravitino and the swampland

evidence.text: Expand around the original minimum, differentiate the added inverse-volume potential, and test the resulting displacement against the local expansion and mass sensitivity. Transport the AdS tower only when these checks hold.

sources.title: Localized gravity, de Sitter, and the Horizon Criterion

evidence.text: Solve bulk Einstein equations, Israel boundary conditions, and scalar equations for spherical and spatially flat brane embeddings. Analyze signals traveling through the bulk as well as along the induced brane geometry.

sources.title: Quantum Breaking Bound on de Sitter and Swampland

evidence.text: Identify the interaction, its effective coupling, and its characteristic classical time; estimate the quantum break-time; then compare the system's escape time with that deadline. The source applies this operation to gravitational patches and scalar-potential evolution.

sources.title: Fuzzy Instantons in Landscape and Swampland: Review of the Hartle–Hawking Wave Function and Several Applications

evidence.text: Which potentials permit classical histories from Hartle–Hawking fuzzy instantons, do their probabilities favor sufficient inflation, and can fast-roll hilltops or extensions beyond the no-boundary proposal accommodate conjectural quantum-gravity constraints?

sources.title: Stochastic Survival near Swampland Boundaries

evidence.text: Given independently justified stochastic dynamics and operational EFT-control conditions, what fraction of fluctuating cosmological histories remain controlled for a prescribed duration, when do they fail, and how does survival conditioning bias their dynamics?

sources.title: Interplay between Swampland and Bayesian Machine Learning in constraining cosmological models

evidence.text: Can inequalities proposed as quantum-gravity consistency conditions supply useful constraints on a cosmological expansion history before observational data enter the analysis, and can those constraints predict subsequent agreement with expansion-rate observations?

sources.title: A (Strictly) Contemporary Perspective on Trans-Planckian Censorship

evidence.text: How should a cosmological description interpret late classical observables whose formal mode ancestry lies above its initial ultraviolet cutoff? The problem arises only for suitable expansion and classicalization histories.

sources.title: Decoupling in an expanding universe: Backreaction barely constrains short distance effects in the CMB

evidence.text: Can high-energy corrections to cosmological initial conditions produce observable CMB signatures while respecting gravitational backreaction, and over what time interval is the boundary effective theory valid?

sources.title: On Efforts to Decouple Early Universe Cosmology and Quantum Gravity Phenomenology

evidence.text: Does generalized cosmic censorship justify pursuing early-universe cosmology independently of quantum-gravity phenomenology, and what assumptions about information propagation underlie an everywhere-classical resolution of the Big Bang?

sources.title: Holographic origin of TCC and the distance conjecture

evidence.text: Can complete boundary observables constrain cosmological expansion and asymptotic particle masses, thereby explaining parts of TCC and the distance conjecture?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: How can a theory with many low-energy realizations make falsifiable predictions? The lecture proposes statistical typicality tests and exclusion of unrealizable effective theories, while emphasizing uncertainty about representative samples and broken-supersymmetry vacua.

sources.title: Trans-Planckian censorship conjecture from the swampland distance conjecture

evidence.text: Does the emergence of light states at large scalar-field distance constrain cosmological expansion strongly enough to prevent initially trans-Planckian fluctuations from crossing the Hubble horizon?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: The framework asks how restrictions motivated by quantum gravity constrain scalar potentials used for cosmological inflation.

sources.title: Is the trans-Planckian censorship a swampland conjecture?

evidence.text: Can a probability-based UV criterion assume our Universe is typical when its small cosmological constant may require a rare history? The source asks whether anthropic weighting resolves this difficulty or adds another arbitrary ingredient.

destination.title: Fakeon classical dynamics and causality
destination.question: How does fakeon projection determine classical gravitational equations and the range or observability of their microcausality violation?
destination.summary: Exact FLRW resummation and possible macroscopic causal effects are separate questions within the same prescription.

assumptions: The projection prescription is part of the investigated framework.
conventions: Do not identify projection with an instability calculation in an unprojected ghost theory.
includes: Light-cone, boost and gravitational-radiation effects as alternatives under examination

sources.title: Fakeons and the classicization of quantum gravity: the FLRW metric

evidence.text: How does projecting fake degrees of freedom out of a quantum theory determine its classical limit, and when can that perturbative projection be resummed exactly for FLRW cosmology rather than yielding only asymptotic classical equations?

sources.title: Fakeons and microcausality: light cones, gravitational waves and the Hubble constant

evidence.text: Can the classical microcausality violation induced by fakeon projection become observable or propagate to macroscopic distances through light-cone effects, Lorentz boosts or gravitational radiation, and how does cosmological expansion affect it?

sources.title: Fakeons and the classicization of quantum gravity: the FLRW metric

evidence.text: Studies higher-derivative mechanical models using principal-value limits for coincident thresholds, repeated fakeon averages, harmonic resummation and iterative anharmonic expansions. Coefficient matching and numerical comparisons of truncation orders illustrate asymptotic behavior.

sources.title: Fakeons and microcausality: light cones, gravitational waves and the Hubble constant

evidence.text: Expand the gravitational equations to first order in κ and separate Einstein and fakeon contributions. For constant H, resum the Fourier-space operator and implement projection by removing on-shell delta-function contributions.

sources.title: Fakeons and the classicization of quantum gravity: the FLRW metric

evidence.text: Uses the imported fakeon prescription: quantum amplitudes undergo nonanalytic average continuation at fakeon thresholds, while the classical inverse operator is the half-sum of retarded and advanced Green functions, ⟨A⟩X = [(X⁻¹)ret + (X⁻¹)adv]A/2.

sources.title: Fakeons and the classicization of quantum gravity: the FLRW metric

evidence.text: Derives FLRW equations through a reduced action retaining both a(t) and lapse b(t), varying before setting b = 1. The stated equivalence conditions require independent reduced equations and algebraic relations connecting the remaining full equations.

sources.title: Fakeons and microcausality: light cones, gravitational waves and the Hubble constant

evidence.text: Use principal-value Fourier Green functions, Wick rotation and Bessel-function representations; resolve the source into temporal frequencies and estimate causal and time-symmetric approximations with relative L² errors.

conventions: Electric/magnetic frames, embedding tensors and supersymmetry conventions are source-specific
excludes: A common gauging or universal higher-dimensional realization

evidence.text: Which AdS vacua of four-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity preserve N>2 supersymmetries, which gaugings support them, and what mass spectra and AdS supermultiplets realize their partial supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: ${\mathcal{N}=(8,0)}$ AdS vacua of three-dimensional supergravity

evidence.text: Which half-maximal three-dimensional gauged supergravities admit fully supersymmetric chiral N=(8,0) AdS3 vacua for n≤8 matter multiplets, and what are their embedding tensors, gauge groups, fluctuation spectra and possible embeddings into maximal supergravity?

sources.title: New methods for old problems: vacua of maximal D = 7 supergravities

evidence.text: Can numerical optimization of embedding-tensor constraints, followed by analytical reconstruction, discover and characterize vacua across maximal seven-dimensional gauged supergravities without selecting one gauging in advance?

sources.title: Trombone gaugings of five-dimensional maximal supergravity

evidence.text: How are general five-dimensional maximal supergravities with gauged trombone scaling specified, which gaugings fit inside R+×SL(2,R)×SL(6,R), and what supersymmetric AdS vacua and spectra occur in a concrete member?

sources.title: The $ \mathcal{N}>2 $ supersymmetric AdS vacua in maximal supergravity

evidence.text: Imposes Killing-spinor conditions in an adapted index basis, reduces the quadratic constraints using SO(3)d singlets, and uses Mathematica to scan real solutions. The inequivalent massive-gravitino decompositions considered are 5, 3+1+1, and 2+2+1.

sources.title: ${\mathcal{N}=(8,0)}$ AdS vacua of three-dimensional supergravity

evidence.text: Compute scalar masses from the potential Hessian and other masses from embedding-tensor-dependent fermion and vector matrices. Project out Goldstone scalars and goldstini, then organize physical fluctuations into supermultiplets using conformal dimensions.

sources.title: New methods for old problems: vacua of maximal D = 7 supergravities

evidence.text: Minimizes a sum of squared constraint polynomials using CMA-ES, with genetic mutation/crossover to escape local minima and parallel initial populations. A barrier excludes the trivial zero embedding tensor; Gaussian penalties discourage revisiting previously found points.

sources.title: Trombone gaugings of five-dimensional maximal supergravity

evidence.text: The embedding tensor has conventional Θ components in the 351 and trombone ϑ components in the 27 of E6(6). Linear constraints enforce maximal-supersymmetry compatibility; quadratic constraints enforce closure of the gauge generators into a Lie algebra.

sources.title: The $ \mathcal{N}>2 $ supersymmetric AdS vacua in maximal supergravity

evidence.text: The going-to-the-origin method uses scalar-manifold homogeneity to move a vacuum to φ=0 while transforming its embedding tensor. Supersymmetry and vacuum equations then become algebraic conditions on the SU(8) tensors Aij and Ai jkl, in representations 36 and 420.

sources.title: The $ \mathcal{N}>2 $ supersymmetric AdS vacua in maximal supergravity

evidence.text: Identifies gauge algebras through Cartan-Killing signatures and compares traces of powers of an E7(7)-covariant quartic tensor to determine deformation parameters. Evaluates bosonic and fermionic mass matrices and matches their eigenvalues to AdS supermultiplets.

sources.title: Chiral Supergravity

evidence.text: Can chiral gravity be extended supersymmetrically, with explicit gravitino modes and conserved charges demonstrating chirality and perturbative AdS3 stability under suitable boundary conditions?

sources.title: AdS$_9$ solutions in type II supergravities

evidence.text: Can type II supergravity support non-supersymmetric AdS9 geometries warped over an interval, and what do endpoint asymptotics, Euclidean actions and holographic observables imply about their possible quantum-gravity interpretation?

sources.title: AdS$_{8}$ solutions in type II supergravity

evidence.text: Can non-supersymmetric AdS8 compactifications provide string-theoretic evidence for unitary interacting seven-dimensional CFTs, beyond the dimensions admitting superconformal theories?

sources.title: More on Massive 3D Supergravity

evidence.text: Can cosmological NMG and GMG arise as genuine bosonic truncations of N = 1 supergravity, which AdS vacua are supersymmetric, and under what conditions are their linearized excitations perturbatively unitary?

sources.title: Exploiting N=2 in consistent coset reductions of type IIA

evidence.text: Can left-invariant type IIA coset reductions be justified as consistent truncations, and can their four-dimensional N=2 structure constrain supersymmetric, nonsupersymmetric and de Sitter vacua, including perturbative string-loop effects?

sources.title: Uplifting non-compact gauged supergravities

evidence.text: How can known de Sitter vacua of regular noncompact maximal gauged supergravity be embedded into eleven-dimensional supergravity, including vacua requiring internal flux? The paper seeks a nonlinear metric and three-form ansatz and a generalized-geometric explanation for it.

sources.title: Halving ISO(7) supergravity

evidence.text: Can half-maximal truncations make dyonic ISO(7) supergravity tractable while retaining its important supersymmetric vacua, and what additional gaugings and AdS extrema arise?

sources.title: Holographic RG flows in $N=4$ SCFTs from half-maximal gauged supergravity

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric AdS4 vacua, scalar spectra and domain-wall flows arise in semisimple, dyonically gauged N = 4 supergravity, and how might they describe relevant deformations of three-dimensional N = 4 SCFTs?

sources.title: Vacua of maximal gauged D = 3 supergravities

evidence.text: Which vacua occur in semisimple maximal three-dimensional gauged supergravities, what supersymmetries and fluctuation spectra do they possess, and how do their stability patterns differ from higher-dimensional examples?

sources.title: New Supersymmetric and Stable, Non-Supersymmetric Phases in Supergravity and Holographic Field Theory

evidence.text: Can numerically discovered AdS critical points of four-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity be characterized analytically, connected by supersymmetric holographic flows, and tested for stability against the full scalar spectrum, including modes outside small truncations?

sources.title: Maximally Supersymmetric AdS Solutions and their Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Which gaugings admit maximally supersymmetric AdS_D vacua for D≥4, and which continuous scalar deformations preserve their supersymmetry?

sources.title: Type IIA AdS(4) compactifications on cosets, interpolations and domain walls

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional cosets with left-invariant strict SU(3) structures support supersymmetric type IIA AdS4 vacua, with or without smeared sources? Can these vacua be connected by supersymmetric domain walls or interpolated to a G2-holonomy lift?

sources.title: Kaluza-Klein Supergravity 2025

evidence.text: What do eleven-dimensional supergravity compactifications, especially round and squashed seven-spheres, teach about surviving supersymmetry, gauge symmetry, vacuum stability, consistent truncations and complete Kaluza–Klein spectra? This is a retrospective review with updates on spectral methods.

sources.title: $ \mathcal{N} $ = 2 CFT$_{3}$’s from $ \mathcal{N} $ = 4 gauged supergravity

evidence.text: Can deformations of four-dimensional half-maximal ISO(3) × ISO(3) gauged supergravity provide holographic evidence for interconnected N = 2 CFT3 conformal manifolds, including N = 3 and N = 4 enhancement loci?

sources.title: Scale-separated vacua with extended supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can classical massive Type IIA compactifications produce parametrically scale-separated AdS3 vacua preserving extended supersymmetry, with a consistent three-dimensional N=2 effective description?

sources.title: A cornucopia of AdS$_{5}$ vacua

evidence.text: Which AdS5 critical points occur in five-dimensional maximal SO(6) gauged supergravity, what supersymmetry and scalar stability do they have, and how many can be captured by tractable consistent truncations?

sources.title: Maximally Supersymmetric AdS Solutions in Gauged Supergravity

evidence.text: Which classical backgrounds preserve every supercharge of a gauged or otherwise deformed supergravity, which gaugings admit pure AdS vacua, and which continuous scalar deformations preserve their supersymmetry? The holographic motivation is to constrain conformal manifolds of dual SCFTs.

sources.title: Consistent subsectors of maximal supergravity and wrapped M5-branes

evidence.text: Which sufficient conditions make invariant subsectors of maximal four-dimensional gauged supergravity consistent when the invariance group lies outside the gauge group, and can a new maximal theory encompass wrapped-M5 AdS4 models and their enlarged mass spectra?

sources.title: Universal Kaluza-Klein reductions of type IIB to N=4 supergravity in five dimensions

evidence.text: Can universal consistent type IIB reductions on arbitrary HK4 × S1 and SE5 retain the massive breathing-mode sector, and what five-dimensional supergravity, gauging and AdS vacua result?

sources.title: New (maximal) gauged supergravities

evidence.text: Review how maximal classical gauged supergravities, their vacua, and their consistent higher-dimensional origins can be constructed and classified, with applications to holography.

sources.title: Shadow multiplets in AdS(4) / CFT(3) and the superHiggs mechanism: Hints of new shadow supergravities

evidence.text: Why do Freund–Rubin Kaluza–Klein spectra contain universal long multiplets with rational dimensions, and can the N=3 graviton's massive gravitino shadow be understood through N=4→N=3 super-Higgs breaking? Does its spectrum require a new supergravity formulation?

sources.title: Tri-Sasakian consistent reduction

evidence.text: Can eleven-dimensional supergravity on any seven-dimensional tri-Sasakian manifold admit a universal consistent truncation retaining massive modes, and what four-dimensional gauged supergravity, AdS vacua and subtruncations result?

sources.title: Triality and the consistent reductions on AdS$_{3}$ × S$^{3}$

evidence.text: Can SO(4,4) triality generate inequivalent consistent sphere truncations of six-dimensional supergravity, exposing additional AdS3 vacua and their parameter-dependent Kaluza–Klein spectra?

sources.title: Consistent truncations around half-maximal AdS$_{5}$ vacua of 11-dimensional supergravity

evidence.text: Which consistent truncations around eleven-dimensional AdS₅ vacua preserving 16 supercharges yield five-dimensional half-maximal gauged supergravity with vector multiplets, and what restricts their matter content and gaugings?
